messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Problems to compile a simple Skew-Normal regression
parts:
It looks like the skew-normal distribution define in TMB is
standardized (i.e. based on a standard N(0,1) distribution).

I'm guessing that you would want to standardize your response
variable before feeding it to the skew-normal.

mu = beta0 + beta1*x;
sd = exp(logsd);
y0 = (y-mu)/sd;
nll = -sum(y0, alpha, true);


(This is assuming that you have defined mu as a vector, sd as a scalar,
and logsd as an additional parameter.)

Just guessing, though.


====

template <class Type>
Type dsn(Type x, Type alpha, int give_log=0)
{

if(!give_log) return 2 * dnorm(x,Type(0),Type(1),0) *
pnorm(alpha*x);
else return log(2.0) + log(dnorm(x,Type(0),Type(1),0)) +
log(pnorm(alpha*x));
}


http://kaskr.github.io/adcomp/distributions__R_8hpp_source.html

messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Problems to compile a simple Skew-Normal regression
parts:
Yes, it appears to be based on the standard normal. The road to finding out this is by the way:
 
http://kaskr.github.io/adcomp/
 
and typing "dsn" in the search field. This brings  up the documentation from which you can go to the code.

You can transform the variable, but you must use the transformation formula for probability densities.
In the terminology of https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skew_normal_distribution
the transformation formula:

https://wikimedia.org/api/rest_v1/media/math/render/svg/f6b462dbbe3ef89df7334f0e198056637ed8e2fc

which can be implemented as dsn((x-xi)/omega,alpha,true)

This should probably go into the documentation.

I hope this helps.

Hans

Hello, 

I am adding onto this thread as it is the only instance where I find skew normal distributions mentioned!

I am trying to define a skew normal density function in TMB. In R, this looks like:

# Define parameters for skew normal given mean mu, standard deviation sigma, and skew parameter alpha

delta <- alpha/sqrt(1+(alpha^2))

omega <- sqrt(sigma^2/(1-(2*delta^2)/pi))

xi <- mu - omega*delta*sqrt(2/pi)

# Skew normal density function

dskewnorm <- function(x, xi, omega, alpha){
  (2/omega) * dnorm((x-xi)/omega) * pnorm(alpha*((x-xi)/omega))
}

And I have verified that this function matches skew normal density functions in packages sn and brms.

I am having trouble implementing this in TMB. When I try to create my own function (outside of the objective function) like this:

template<class Type>
Type dskewnorm(Type x, Type xi, Type omega, Type alpha){
  return 2/omega * dnorm((x-xi/omega), 0, 1) * pnorm(alpha*((x - xi)/ omega));
}

I get the error "deduced conflicting types for parameter 'Type' ('tmbutils::vector<CppAD::AD<double> >' vs. 'CppAD::AD<double>'"

This appears to be associated with pnorm (I can get the dnorm bit to work). Is there any way to convince pnorm to accept a regular vector or double instead of a CppAD object?

I've tried to pull out the source code (in atomic and Rmath) but run into the same problems. I also tried using the built-in function dsn() but that function only accepts two parameters (x and alpha) and I didn't get the values that I expected -- is there a way to adapt that function for my purposes?

Any advice would be much appreciated!

Cheers, 

Eiren

messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Problems to compile a simple Skew-Normal regression
parts:
Thanks for your help Joaquin and Hans! Just in case others need to do this, here is what I ended up with following the advice in this thread.

The function dsn() is standardized to N(0,1) and calculated as: 2 * dnorm(x,Type(0),Type(1),0) * pnorm(alpha*x); 
The density of the general skew normal is given by this equation, where delta, omega, and xi are parameters that can be solved for given some mean and variance according to the equations on the right side of this wikipedia article. So, to adapt the TMB function dsn() to give the density of x given mu, sigma, and alpha, we basically need to substitute (x - xi)/omega in for x and divide by omega so that the TMB function matches the definition of the skew normal density. In TMB, this looks like:

Given mean mu, standard deviation sigma, and slant parameter alpha:

// convert mu, sigma, alpha to parameters needed for skew normal

  delta = alpha/sqrt(1+pow(alpha,2));
   
  omega = sqrt(pow(sigma,2)/(1-(2*pow(delta,2))/pi));
 
  xi = mu - omega*delta*sqrt(2/pi);

// calculate density over values of x

for (int i = 0; i < nx; i++){
d(i) = dsn((x(i) - xi)/omega, alpha, false)/omega;
}
